title: Shakshuka
description: Eggs poached in a thick, smoky tomato and pepper sauce until the whites are set and the yolks still run. Bring the pan to the table and mop it up with bread.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a frying pan about 24cm wide over a medium heat. Add the onion and pepper with a pinch of salt and cook, stirring now and then, until very soft and starting to colour.
Add the garlic, cumin, both paprikas and the chilli flakes and stir for a minute until fragrant. Stir in the tomato puree.

Pour in the chopped tomatoes and water, then add the sugar and salt. Simmer, stirring occasionally, until the sauce is thick enough that a spoon dragged through it leaves a clear trail. Taste and adjust the seasoning now, before the eggs go in.
steps.tip: A thin sauce will not hold the eggs in place, so keep going until it is properly thick.

steps.text: Turn the heat down to low. Make four wells in the sauce with the back of a spoon and crack an egg into each. Season the eggs with a little salt.
steps.tip: Crack each egg into a cup first if you are worried about shell or a broken yolk.

steps.text: Cover the pan and cook gently until the whites are just set and the yolks still wobble. Start checking after 5 minutes, as the eggs carry on cooking once off the heat.
Scatter with the feta and coriander and serve straight from the pan with the toasted bread.

tips: No lid for your pan? A baking tray or a large plate laid over the top does the job.
To serve four, double everything and use a 30cm pan so the eggs have room.

substitutions.note: add a spoonful on top at the end
stir 1 to 2 tsp in with the tomato puree

storage: The sauce keeps for 4 days in the fridge without the eggs. Reheat it until bubbling, then add fresh eggs.
author: Simmer
